meta.title: Top 100 Health Food Stores 2026
meta.subtitle: The stores that define healthy-food retail — ranked. Celebrity grocers, working co-ops, organic pioneers, farm shops, and the zero-waste new wave.

scoreModel.name: Store Score
scoreModel.gate: Specific, currently-operating physical stores where health-food retail is the core business. Chains enter through individual locations judged as places — never as a brand in the abstract. Restaurants and online-only sellers do not qualify.
scoreModel.notes: Reach is log-scaled and recomputed from each store's researched follower counts. The five judgment factors — legacy, selection, experience, community, destination — are calibrated across research segments so no category is scored on an easier curve. Counts marked verified were browser-checked at the listed date; the rest are approximate.

meta.disclaimer: Details are editorial estimates (2026) and the ranking is reviewed monthly. Inclusion is not an endorsement; stores move, renovate, and close — check before you travel.

entries.name: Erewhon Beverly Blvd (Fairfax)
entries.who: The chain's original store, a 1968 macrobiotic shop turned ultra-premium celebrity grocery flagship at 7660 Beverly Blvd since 1991.
entries.why: The most photographed, most celebrity-trafficked health food store in the country, credited with inventing the $20 smoothie era.

entries.name: Daylesford Organic (Kingham farm shop)
entries.who: Organic farm shop built around Carole Bamford's Cotswolds farm, with an on-site creamery, café and cookery school.
entries.why: Britain's best-known organic farm-shop destination; set the template for farm-to-table retail as a day out.

entries.name: Rainbow Grocery Cooperative
entries.who: Worker-owned natural foods co-op since 1975, no outside investors, heavy bulk and vegetarian focus.
entries.why: One of the last surviving worker-owned grocery co-ops and a fixture of San Francisco food culture.

entries.name: Erewhon Calabasas
entries.who: The chain's 2014 second-generation location in the Kardashian-adjacent Calabasas foothills, one of Erewhon's largest stores with a spacious hot bar.
entries.why: Independently iconic as a celebrity-spotting destination in its own right, distinct in clientele and layout from the Fairfax original.

entries.name: Berkeley Bowl
entries.who: Independent produce-and-grocery market, two locations, open since 1977.
entries.why: The produce range and sourcing set the reference point other independents get measured against.

entries.name: Whole Foods Market (Austin flagship)
entries.who: The mothership flagship store blocks from the original 1980 North Lamar location where four Austin natural-food retailers launched the entire natural-supermarket format.
entries.why: The store that invented the natural-foods supermarket as a category, surviving a 1981 flood to build what became a $20B+ business.

entries.name: Hansalim
entries.who: South Korea's largest organic consumer cooperative, founded in 1986, with retail shops across Seoul serving well over a million members.
entries.why: Defined the direct farmer-to-consumer organic movement in Korea; the world's biggest cooperative of its kind.

entries.name: Park Slope Food Coop
entries.who: Member-labor food co-op with 16,700+ members and one storefront, open since 1973.
entries.why: Defined the American working-co-op model — every member works a shift, and it still runs on that rule alone.

entries.name: White Oak Pastures General Store
entries.who: General store on a sixth-generation regenerative cattle ranch, selling the farm's own grass-fed beef, poultry and tallow soap on-site.
entries.why: A pilgrimage site for the regenerative-agriculture movement, built around a documented zero-waste, whole-animal model.

entries.name: Green Common
entries.who: Hong Kong's leading plant-based grocery-and-cafe flagship, a two-storey concept in Central with a grocery, deli and restaurant.
entries.why: The regional reference for plant-based retail, backed by the Green Monday movement.

entries.name: Shelburne Farms Farm Store & Welcome Center
entries.who: Farm store on a historic 1,400-acre Lake Champlain estate turned nonprofit, selling farmhouse cheddar and maple syrup made on-site.
entries.why: One of the oldest working-farm retail experiences in the US, pairing legacy architecture with hands-on food production.

entries.name: PCC Community Markets
entries.who: Nation's largest consumer-owned food co-op, 117,000+ members, 16 certified-organic stores since 1953.
entries.why: Started as a 15-family buying club and scaled into the biggest co-op grocery network in the country.

entries.name: Crayon House
entries.who: Organic cafe, grocery and bookstore in Aoyama, open since 1976 as a combined publishing house and health-food pioneer.
entries.why: One of Tokyo's oldest organic institutions, still open and still mixing books, toys and organic food under one roof.

entries.name: Alnatura Super Natur Markt (Darmstadt)
entries.who: Flagship 'Super Natur Markt' of Germany's biggest organic brand, sited on Alnatura's landmark clay-and-timber headquarters campus.
entries.why: Showcase store for Alnatura's sustainable-building philosophy; the campus itself is a minor architectural destination.

entries.name: Polyface Farm Store
entries.who: On-farm store at Joel Salatin's regenerative farm, selling pastured meat, eggs and dairy direct from the pastures.
entries.why: The farm store that put regenerative grazing and direct-farm retail on the map, made famous by The Omnivore's Dilemma and Food, Inc.

entries.name: Natural House Aoyama
entries.who: Japan's original organic supermarket chain (about 30 stores nationwide), anchored by its Aoyama store near Omotesando.
entries.why: The store that brought organic and macrobiotic groceries into mainstream Tokyo shopping.

entries.name: The Wedge Community Co-op
entries.who: Founded 1974 in a Minneapolis basement; now one of the largest single-site natural foods co-ops in the US.
entries.why: A founding-era Twin Cities co-op that helped seed the Midwest natural-foods movement.

entries.name: Whole Foods Market Kensington
entries.who: The UK's largest Whole Foods Market, occupying the former Barkers department store on Kensington High Street.
entries.why: The chain's most architecturally significant UK site; the grand food-hall building pulls in visitors beyond weekly shoppers.

entries.name: Los Poblanos Farm Shop
entries.who: Farm shop on a historic lavender farm and inn, set in restored 1930s dairy barns, selling lavender goods, Farm Foods pantry items and baked goods.
entries.why: A working farm's retail core built into real historic architecture, drawing people who plan trips around it.

entries.name: Moon Juice (Melrose Ave, LA)
entries.who: Adaptogen-and-cold-press-juice shop opened 2011 by Amanda Chantal Bacon; the original storefront that launched the 'dust' wellness-supplement category.
entries.why: A tiny shop that became a reference point for the entire US adaptogen and wellness-tonic industry.

entries.name: Ocean Beach People's Food Co-op
entries.who: San Diego's only grocery co-op, founded 1971 as a buying club, fully certified-organic produce department.
entries.why: The city's sole surviving food co-op, still tracing straight back to a 1971 buying club.

entries.name: Planet Organic (Westbourne Grove)
entries.who: Organic supermarket chain founded 1995, now around ten London stores under founder ownership.
entries.why: Pioneered UK organic-supermarket retail; survived a 2023 insolvency and relaunched smaller under its original founders.
entries.warning: Entered administration in May 2023; sold to a company backed by its founders, with four of fourteen stores closed in the process.

entries.name: Infinity Foods
entries.who: Workers' co-operative wholefood shop and bakery trading since 1971, one of Britain's oldest surviving co-ops.
entries.why: Founding-era co-op culture, still worker-owned and run on collective decision-making more than five decades on.

entries.name: Ruohonjuuri
entries.who: Finland's leading health-food chain, trading since 1982, selling natural foods, supplements and organic cosmetics.
entries.why: Set the template for health-food retail in Finland and still runs the country's widest store network in the category.

entries.name: Hanover Co-op Food Stores
entries.who: Consumer co-op founded 1936 as a 17-family buying club; now three stores, a market, and a service center.
entries.why: Among the oldest surviving consumer co-ops in the country, still owned by the community that started it.

entries.name: Unicorn Grocery
entries.who: Worker-owned wholefood co-op in Chorlton, trading since 1996, known for bulk organic produce and affordable pricing.
entries.why: A model of co-operative retail with a genuinely loyal local membership and strict ethical-sourcing standards.

entries.name: La Louve
entries.who: Member-run food cooperative in the Park Slope Food Coop mold, open since 2016; members work shifts in exchange for low prices.
entries.why: France's best-known food co-op, widely written up abroad as a working alternative to conventional grocery retail.

entries.name: Naturalia (Boulevard Magenta)
entries.who: France's pioneering organic supermarket chain, opened on Boulevard Magenta in 1973 and now over 250 stores nationwide.
entries.why: One of Europe's first organic-supermarket concepts; helped move organic food from niche shop to mainstream aisle.

entries.name: FARMshop
entries.who: Bakery-and-market inside the 1948 Brentwood Country Mart, stocking curated organic produce, cheeses, chocolate and wine alongside its restaurant.
entries.why: A market built directly into an LA architectural landmark, functioning as both grocer and neighborhood ritual.

entries.name: The Alchemist's Kitchen
entries.who: SoHo apothecary and elixir bar selling herbal tinctures, medicinal mushrooms, CBD and wellness tonics, with in-house herbalist consultations.
entries.why: Helped define the modern plant-medicine retail concept that later spread across US wellness culture.

entries.name: City Market, Onion River Co-op
entries.who: Burlington's community-owned grocery co-op, successor to the original Onion River Co-op buying club.
entries.why: Vermont's flagship food co-op, anchoring one of the most co-op-dense food scenes in the country.

entries.name: The Big Carrot Community Market
entries.who: Worker-owned natural food market on the Danforth, organic and non-GMO since 1983, now two locations.
entries.why: Toronto's longest-running worker-owned natural grocer, with a juice bar and wellness boutique built in.

entries.name: Willy Street Co-op
entries.who: Community-owned natural foods co-op with three Madison locations, founded 1972.
entries.why: A Midwest anchor co-op with a following bigger than its store count suggests.

entries.name: Sevananda Natural Foods Market
entries.who: Atlanta's only cooperative grocery, open since 1974 in Little Five Points, 4,000+ member-owners.
entries.why: A 50-year survivor and the sole co-op grocery left standing in a major Southern city.

entries.name: MOM's Organic Market (Rockville)
entries.who: The original location of the MOM's Organic Market chain, founded 1987, now the DC area's largest organic grocery brand.
entries.why: The founding store of a regional organic-grocery chain built on a strict banned-ingredients list.

entries.name: Negozio Leggero (Turin founding store)
entries.who: The world's first zero-waste, refill-by-weight grocery network, founded in Turin in 2009.
entries.why: Originated the loose-goods refill retail model that zero-waste stores worldwide have since copied.

entries.name: Anima Mundi Apothecary
entries.who: Herbal apothecary and tonic bar founded in Brooklyn, now with SoHo and Los Angeles locations, known for adaptogenic elixirs and vivid packaging.
entries.why: One of the most photographed herbal apothecaries in the US, credited with mainstreaming the modern tonic-bar aesthetic.

entries.name: Lemon Farm
entries.who: Thailand's pioneering organic supermarket chain, founded 1999 and now 14-plus branches with in-store organic cafes.
entries.why: Defined organic retail in Thailand and helped build the country's organic-farmer supply network.

entries.name: Organic Foods & Cafe
entries.who: The Middle East's pioneering organic supermarket and cafe, founded 2004, with locations across Dubai.
entries.why: Introduced organic retail to the Gulf region and remains its most established organic grocer.

entries.name: Wellness Warehouse
entries.who: South Africa's leading wellness-and-organic retail chain, flagship on Cape Town's Kloof Street, with stores nationwide.
entries.why: Defined organic and supplement retail in South Africa, closest thing the country has to a health-food department store.

entries.name: Better Food
entries.who: Independent organic grocer with four Bristol shops, each paired with its own cafe.
entries.why: A fixture of Bristol's ethical-food scene since the early 2000s, known for the shop-plus-cafe format at every branch.

entries.name: Country Life
entries.who: Health-food store, bakery and vegetarian restaurant chain that says it was there when organic food first reached the Czech market; six shops plus restaurants and a cafe in and around Prague.
entries.why: A pioneer of the Czech organic-food movement, still operating its original Old Town shop and restaurant today.

entries.name: Wheatsville Food Co-op
entries.who: Austin's oldest food co-op, two full-service member-owned grocery stores, open since 1976.
entries.why: A longtime local institution running a full grocery format on co-op ownership.

entries.name: Seward Community Co-op
entries.who: Member-owned natural foods co-op with two Minneapolis stores, sister institution to the Wedge.
entries.why: A long-running Twin Cities co-op built on volunteer culture and community programming.

entries.name: Hunger Mountain Co-op
entries.who: Vermont's capital-city natural food co-op: 10,000 member-owners and 400 local vendors on Stone Cutters Way.
entries.why: A dense concentration of member-owners for a small city, and Vermont's local-vendor showcase.

entries.name: Mr Vitamins
entries.who: Independent Australian vitamin and supplement retailer since the 1970s, stocking supplements, sports nutrition and healthy foods.
entries.why: A rare independent supplement retailer that outlasted chain competitors by building deep category expertise.

entries.name: The Source Bulk Foods
entries.who: Originator of Australia's zero-waste bulk-foods grocery format, founded 2012 near Byron Bay, now 50-plus stores including overseas expansion.
entries.why: Created the bring-your-own-container, buy-by-weight retail model now copied worldwide.

entries.name: BEES coop
entries.who: Member-owned cooperative supermarket in Brussels, open since 2015, run on volunteer member shifts.
entries.why: Belgium's flagship food co-op and a reference point for the member-run grocery model in continental Europe.

entries.name: Honest Weight Food Co-op
entries.who: Large all-volunteer-rooted natural foods co-op on Watervliet Avenue, marking fifty years in 2026.
entries.why: One of the biggest member-owned co-ops in the Northeast, still built on working membership.

entries.name: NaturaSì (Verona)
entries.who: Italy's largest organic supermarket chain, part of the EcorNaturaSì group and rooted in Verona with 300-plus stores.
entries.why: Anchors Italy's organic retail market with strict own-label sourcing standards across a national store network.

entries.name: ZERO Market
entries.who: Colorado's package-free grocery pioneer inside the Stanley Marketplace, stocking over 1,200 bulk and zero-waste pantry, body-care and cleaning goods since 2017.
entries.why: One of the earliest and longest-running zero-waste grocery stores in the US, a model newer package-free shops point back to.

entries.name: Down to Earth Organic and Natural (King St, Honolulu)
entries.who: Hawaii's homegrown organic-and-vegetarian grocer, founded 1977 in Wailuku, Maui; the King Street, Honolulu store opened the same year and remains the flagship after a 2008 renovation.
entries.why: The islands' definitive health-food retailer, running community farmers' markets and free senior meals since its earliest days.

entries.name: iCOOP Natural Dream
entries.who: Retail arm of iCOOP, South Korea's largest consumer cooperative federation, selling organic and natural foods to its member base.
entries.why: Anchors one of Asia's biggest working consumer co-op networks, with a store finder pointing to dozens of member locations.

entries.name: Davis Food Co-op
entries.who: Member-owned grocery co-op on G Street, open since 1972 with over 8,000 member households.
entries.why: A textbook college-town co-op: five decades of local ownership and farm-direct sourcing.

entries.name: Weavers Way Co-op
entries.who: Philadelphia's neighborhood grocer co-op since 1973, now spanning seven locations incl. a farm market.
entries.why: Grown from one Mt. Airy storefront into a multi-site network without losing its co-op structure.

entries.name: Natural Grocers (Golden/Lakewood, CO origin)
entries.who: Founded 1955 as door-to-door 'Vitamin Cottage' by Margaret and Philip Isely; first storefront opened in Lakewood, CO in 1963, now headquartered nearby in Golden with 165+ US stores.
entries.why: One of the true origin points of the US health-food-store industry, still education-focused after seven decades.

entries.name: Central Market (North Lamar, Austin original)
entries.who: H-E-B's gourmet/natural-foods banner, opened 1994 on North Lamar in Austin, within blocks of Whole Foods' birthplace; built around scratch bakeries, in-house butchers, and market-style produce.
entries.why: Shows a regional chain can build a genuinely premium, foodie-driven natural-foods format without going fully corporate-national.

entries.name: Chorokmaeul (Green Village)
entries.who: Organic co-op supermarket chain with stores across Korea, a sister strand of the country's farm-to-table cooperative movement.
entries.why: A flagship of Korea's organic co-op retail scene, distinct from Hansalim's larger cooperative model.

entries.name: Commonsense Organics
entries.who: Independent organic supermarket group founded in the 1990s, with anchor stores in Wellington's Thorndon and Newtown.
entries.why: A defining institution of New Zealand's organic-food retail culture.

entries.name: La Montanita Co-op
entries.who: Largest food co-op in the Southwest, stores across Albuquerque, Santa Fe, Gallup, and Los Alamos plus its own distribution center.
entries.why: A regional co-op network, not just a single store, built around New Mexico's local-food supply chain.

entries.name: Boise Co-op Market
entries.who: Member-owned natural foods market with a full deli and cafe, a fixture of Boise's food scene.
entries.why: Idaho's reference co-op for organic and local sourcing, with a following well beyond members.

entries.name: La Vie Claire (original Paris shop)
entries.who: France's first organic and health-food store network, founded in 1948, now a nationwide franchise of small shops.
entries.why: Legacy claim to being Europe's original modern health-food retailer, decades ahead of the organic-supermarket boom.

entries.name: Bristol Farms (Rolling Hills Estates original)
entries.who: Upscale Southern California supermarket chain founded 1982 by former wholesale butchers who modeled it on Harrods' food halls; the original store still operates in Rolling Hills Estates.
entries.why: The white-tablecloth end of health-adjacent grocery, long favored by affluent South Bay and Beverly Hills shoppers for its butcher counters and produce theatre.

entries.name: Mother's Market & Kitchen (Costa Mesa original)
entries.who: Organic grocer-and-kitchen opened 1978 by the MacGurn family with backing from a local yoga center; the original Costa Mesa store anchors an 11-store Southern California chain.
entries.why: One of the longest-running organic grocers in the US, built around a yoga/wellness community rather than as a retail play from day one.

entries.name: ThreeSixty
entries.who: Upscale organic supermarket chain in Hong Kong with several stores carrying imported organic and specialty goods.
entries.why: The reference organic supermarket for Hong Kong's health-conscious and expat shoppers.

entries.name: Central Co-op
entries.who: Community-owned natural foods co-op on Capitol Hill, plus a Tacoma location, known for social-justice-minded sourcing.
entries.why: A values-driven co-op distinct from PCC, with a strong Capitol Hill identity.

entries.name: BriarPatch Food Co-op
entries.who: Sierra foothills natural foods co-op founded in 1976, with a second store in Auburn.
entries.why: Nearly fifty years feeding the Gold Country region on local, organic sourcing.

entries.name: Community Natural Foods
entries.who: Calgary natural foods grocer founded 1977 by the Wilkes brothers, now three stores across the city.
entries.why: Alberta's longest-standing independent natural grocer, built around local-supplier sourcing.

entries.name: Jimbo's Naturally (North Park, San Diego original)
entries.who: Organic grocer opened 1984 by Jimbo Someck after leaving a food co-op; the original North Park store anchors a respected six-store San Diego chain now 40+ years old.
entries.why: A San Diego institution known for dropping plastic bags in 2008 and strict local/regenerative-organic sourcing standards.

entries.name: Orga Whole Foods
entries.who: Premium organic grocery chain in Seoul known for imported and domestic organic goods with in-store cafe corners.
entries.why: Seoul's closest equivalent to a Western-style organic supermarket experience.

entries.name: Bin Inn
entries.who: New Zealand bulk wholefoods chain with stores nationwide, trading over 35 years, built around fill-your-own-container bulk bins.
entries.why: Pioneered the bulk-bin, low-packaging shopping format in New Zealand well before it became a trend elsewhere.

entries.name: Angelic Organic Grocer
entries.who: Melbourne health-food grocer and juice bar combining a wholefoods shop with a smoothie/juice counter.
entries.why: A go-to stop for Melbourne's fitness and wellness crowd, more destination than plain grocery run.

entries.name: Outpost Natural Foods Co-op
entries.who: Milwaukee-area natural foods co-op with four stores (Bay View, Wauwatosa, Mequon, Capitol Drive).
entries.why: The main organic anchor for Milwaukee, grown to four stores while staying member-run.

entries.name: Sacramento Natural Foods Co-op
entries.who: Community-owned natural foods grocer on R Street, serving Sacramento since 1973.
entries.why: One of California's older urban co-ops, still community-powered after five decades.

entries.name: Ashland Food Co-op
entries.who: Member-owned grocery co-op serving the Ashland/Rogue Valley area, with deli and bulk sections.
entries.why: The default natural grocer for a small tourist-and-arts town, with a loyal member base.

entries.name: Real Foods
entries.who: Scotland's longest-running organic and special-diet retailer, with two shops on Broughton Street and Brougham Street.
entries.why: A pioneer of natural and special-diet retail in Scotland that has stayed independently run since the 1970s.

entries.name: Mundo Verde
entries.who: Brazil's organic and health-food supermarket chain, founded in the late 1990s with stores across Sao Paulo.
entries.why: Brazil's reference organic supermarket brand, credited with popularizing organic retail nationally.

entries.name: Brattleboro Food Co-op
entries.who: Southern Vermont's community-owned natural foods grocer, open daily with a full cafe.
entries.why: A small-town co-op that punches above its size for a region defined by food co-ops.

entries.name: LPG BioMarkt (Prenzlauer Berg)
entries.who: Berlin's oldest organic supermarket chain, trading since 1994, with ten stores and its own organic Ufa bakery.
entries.why: An early mover in German organic retail; its strict regional (200km) sourcing radius sets it apart from national chains.

entries.name: Ekoplaza (plastic-free aisle store)
entries.who: Dutch organic supermarket chain that opened the world's first plastic-free grocery aisle in 2018.
entries.why: Set a global retail precedent for packaging-free organic shopping that other chains have since copied.

entries.name: Lassens Natural Foods & Vitamins (La Brea, LA)
entries.who: California vitamin-and-natural-foods chain founded 1971 in Camarillo by Oda Lassen; the La Brea, LA store is its best-known city outpost, minutes from Erewhon's original.
entries.why: A family-run, three-generation vitamin-shop institution that predates the celebrity-grocer wave by decades.

entries.name: Lazy Acres Natural Market (Santa Barbara original)
entries.who: Independent organic grocer founded 1991 in Santa Barbara, now a small West Coast banner under the same ownership group (Good Food Holdings) as Bristol Farms and New Seasons.
entries.why: A quieter, neighborhood-scaled organic grocer often named alongside Erewhon and Lassens as an LA-region alternative.

entries.name: Little Farms
entries.who: Singapore's premium organic and health-food grocer chain, multiple locations descending from its original Dempsey Hill store.
entries.why: The default organic grocer for Singapore's health-conscious expat and local shoppers.

entries.name: Leezen
entries.who: Taiwanese organic and sustainable-goods retail chain (Chinese: Li Ren) run as a social enterprise, with stores island-wide.
entries.why: One of Taiwan's most recognized organic grocery names, built explicitly around ethical sourcing rather than just product range.

entries.name: Fresh Earth Store
entries.who: Independent organic grocer and cafe in Johannesburg's Rosebank/Craighall area, running for over a decade.
entries.why: One of Johannesburg's established organic-food destinations, combining a grocery with a sit-down cafe.

entries.name: Bio Company
entries.who: Berlin-founded organic supermarket chain (est. 2003), now around sixty stores across northeastern Germany.
entries.why: Scaled Berlin's organic-retail boom into a regional chain while staying independent of the big German grocers.

entries.name: Alara Wholefoods
entries.who: Independent wholefood shop and mill in King's Cross, trading since 1974, known for its own-milled organic flours and refill counters.
entries.why: One of London's longest-running independent health-food shops, having outlasted the wholesale redevelopment of King's Cross around it.

entries.name: New Seasons Market (Raleigh Hills, Portland original)
entries.who: Grocery chain founded 1999 by three Portland grocery veterans; the Raleigh Hills store was the first of what grew into roughly 20 Pacific Northwest locations.
entries.why: Defined Portland's local-first, sustainability-first grocery identity a decade before it became a national trend.

entries.name: Nature's Basket
entries.who: India's premium gourmet-and-organic grocery chain, active with a rebuilt flagship store in Mumbai's Khar area.
entries.why: The reference for curated imported and organic goods in urban India, though closer to gourmet than pure health-food.

entries.name: Piko Wholefoods
entries.who: Member-owned wholefoods cooperative store trading in Christchurch since the mid-1970s.
entries.why: One of the longest-running food co-ops in New Zealand, still run on member ownership.

entries.name: Bloomingfoods
entries.who: Community-owned co-op grocer since 1976 with multiple Bloomington, Indiana locations.
entries.why: A durable small-city co-op feeding a college town's natural-foods demand for five decades.

entries.name: As Nature Intended
entries.who: Independent London health-food retailer running six shops (Chiswick, Ealing, Balham, Spitalfields, Stratford, Marble Arch) plus a web shop.
entries.why: A rare independent multi-site health-food group that has kept expanding across London while bigger names struggled.

entries.name: Sprouts Farmers Market (Chandler, AZ original)
entries.who: First Sprouts store, opened 2002 by the Boney family (descendants of a 1943 San Diego produce stand); grew into a 400+ store national chain.
entries.why: Proved a mainstream, no-frills organic-and-bulk format could scale nationally without soda aisles or junk-food end caps.

entries.name: Flannerys
entries.who: Queensland-founded organic and health-food supermarket chain with stores across QLD and northern NSW.
entries.why: A long-running regional institution for organic groceries and supplements in southeast Queensland.

entries.name: Mississippi Market
entries.who: St. Paul natural foods co-op with three neighborhood stores across the city.
entries.why: A long-running Twin Cities co-op network known for deep local-vendor relationships.

entries.name: Nude Foods Market
entries.who: Package-free grocery with Boulder and Denver storefronts, selling bulk pantry staples, produce and prepared meals in returnable glass jars.
entries.why: Proves the package-free grocery model can work outside the biggest cities, with a returnable-jar system as its signature.

entries.name: SuperNature
entries.who: Independent organic and health-food store with a cafe corner, a longstanding name in Singapore's wellness retail scene.
entries.why: One of Singapore's older organic specialty grocers, known for curated imported goods.

entries.name: Wild Oats
entries.who: Long-running independent wholefoods shop in Bristol, trading since the 1970s-80s wholefood movement.
entries.why: One of the older independent health-food shops still trading in a city famous for them.

entries.name: SuperBioMarkt
entries.who: Regional organic supermarket chain headquartered in Munster, selling groceries, produce and household goods.
entries.why: One of the established organic-supermarket names in western Germany, running for decades under one brand.

entries.name: Linden Hills Co-op
entries.who: Small neighborhood natural foods co-op in the Linden Hills district, one of the Twin Cities' older co-ops.
entries.why: A tight, walkable neighborhood co-op with deep roots in a famously co-op-dense metro.

bubblingUnder.name: First Alternative Co-op
bubblingUnder.who: Corvallis natural foods co-op with north and south stores, a mainstay of the Willamette Valley co-op scene.
bubblingUnder.why: A steady, member-run counterpart to Oregon's better-known co-ops, serving a college town.

bubblingUnder.name: Remedies Herb Shop
bubblingUnder.who: Small-batch herbal apothecary with Brooklyn and Woodstock, NY stores, curating loose organic herbs and tinctures from about 27 independent herbal makers.
bubblingUnder.why: A community-anchored herb shop that champions small US herbalists over mass-market supplement brands.

bubblingUnder.name: The Green Corner
bubblingUnder.who: Organic and health-food grocery chain in Mexico City with a cafe and juice-bar format across several branches.
bubblingUnder.why: One of Mexico City's go-to spots for organic groceries and a health-food lifestyle scene.

bubblingUnder.name: Healthy Options
bubblingUnder.who: Long-running Philippine health-food and supplement retail chain with mall-based stores nationwide.
bubblingUnder.why: The best-known name in Philippine health-food retail, built over decades of mall presence.

bubblingUnder.name: Terra Madre
bubblingUnder.who: Independent organic grocer and cafe in Melbourne known for its curated pantry and produce selection.
bubblingUnder.why: A neighborhood fixture for Melbourne's organic and slow-food crowd.

bubblingUnder.name: Jackson's Real Food Market
bubblingUnder.who: Independent organic and real-food grocery and cafe in Johannesburg's Craighall Park.
bubblingUnder.why: A community favorite for organic produce and clean-eating groceries in Joburg's northern suburbs.

bubblingUnder.name: Paddock To Pantry
bubblingUnder.who: Family-run New Zealand grocer (formerly trading as Huckleberry) with two physical shops plus nationwide delivery.
bubblingUnder.why: A boutique NZ-owned grocer that rebranded but kept its curated, farm-forward wholefoods focus.

bubblingUnder.name: Lakewinds Food Co-op
bubblingUnder.who: Twin Cities-suburbs natural foods co-op, no membership required, with stores in Chanhassen, Minnetonka, and Richfield.
bubblingUnder.why: An open-to-all co-op model that still built a loyal following across three Minnesota locations.

bubblingUnder.name: The Goods Mart
bubblingUnder.who: A better-for-you corner-store concept in South Williamsburg stocking healthier snacks and drinks from independent, founder-led brands.
bubblingUnder.why: Reinvents the convenience store itself as health-food retail, a genuinely new format for the segment.
